absent: Locking around concurrent trampoline resolution and release.
Computation of trampoline call offsets and decoding of call targets.
Allocator and reclamation details for dynamic trampolines.
Semantics of graph entry bookkeeping, pause control, and dead-state detection.
Exit-handler contract for translating intercepted returns to true addresses.
Cross-CPU visibility and fencing guarantees for runtime text patching.
Full descriptor table layout, privilege levels, and stack selection beyond early setup.
Page-entry flag encodings, caching attributes, and TLB maintenance beyond early construction.
Boot-parameter validation rules and subarchitecture detection beyond dispatch.
Microcode loading effects, ordering constraints, and error handling.
Control-register shadow maintenance and feature probing.
Direct-call and tail-call encoding for saved accumulator values.
Confidential-guest exception handling beyond delegation to helpers.
Frame-pointer encoding details and unwind metadata for trace entries.
Break-range allocator management beyond early zeroing and end-pointer update.

findings.text: The 32-bit kernel entry establishes an early exception table first, then loads bootstrap microcode, clears any early ramdisk mapping, initializes processor control shadow state, validates boot parameters and platform legacy expectations, selects a subarchitecture early setup routine, and finally transfers control to generic kernel initialization without returning.

Compiler-inserted function entry points default to an immediate return. One 64-bit variant instead compares the installed trace function against the idle handler and, when tracing is active, preserves caller state, dispatches through the installed function, restores state, and then reaches the idle handler.

Dynamic trace call sites preserve caller registers, adjust the captured call address by the patched call size, load the parent address and the active trace operations object, invoke a patchable call target defaulting to an idle stub, propagate any handler-modified return address, restore registers, and fall through to patchable graph dispatch.

Register-aware trace entries build a full register frame resembling an interrupt frame, including segment values and flag state, pass the faulting address plus parent plus operations plus frame pointer to a patchable register handler, then restore state while honoring handler-modified instruction pointer and flag values before returning through the shared graph path.

The graph return interceptor saves a small register set and stack reference, asks the generic exit handler for the true caller address, restores saved registers, releases its frame, and transfers control to the returned address through an intra-function call and return sequence preserving return-stack balance across depth-tracking builds.

The early exception dispatcher attempts to create a missing mapping for page faults using the faulting address, delegates virtualization exceptions for confidential guests to dedicated helpers, and otherwise forwards register state and trap number to the generic early fixup path.

Trampoline resolution distinguishes static from allocated handling using FTRACE_OPS_FL_ALLOC_TRAMP. Static choice honors FTRACE_FL_REGS_EN for register preservation and treats FTRACE_GRAPH_ADDR as a graph case selecting prepare_ftrace_return, otherwise deriving from FTRACE_REGS_ADDR or FTRACE_ADDR. Allocated choice offsets from the stored base honoring FTRACE_OPS_FL_SAVE_REGS. Release only frees when allocated and then clears the stored base.

Graph caller control patches a single global dispatch location to point at the active graph handler when enabling and at the idle stub when disabling. Patch generation builds a jump encoding for the target, and installation uses a single-location cross-CPU text update of call size.

Graph entry helpers consult a shared skip predicate and, when tracing should proceed, record function entry through generic graph bookkeeping and replace the saved parent slot with the return interceptor address on success.

Early 32-bit page-table construction fills second-level entries and complete page-table pages up to a limit derived from kernel end plus low-memory table space, records the highest mapped frame number and the new break end, and optionally maps a ramdisk image while saving its virtual start and table range for later teardown.

Early interrupt descriptor setup installs a common early handler for every architectural exception vector, and on 32-bit also installs an ignore handler for remaining vectors, then loads the descriptor table. A small helper builds per-vector descriptor data and installs one entry at a time.

Platform quirk initialization establishes default legacy device expectations and BIOS region handling, adjusts them according to reported hardware subarchitecture, and finally invokes a platform-specific override hook when one is registered.

Early 64-bit mapping creation computes a large-page entry from the requested address plus early flags and installs it through a level-walking allocator creating intermediate tables on demand, reporting success or failure to the caller.
Early state clearing zeroes the kernel uninitialized data range and the bootstrap allocator range before later initialization proceeds.
Default 32-bit early setup wires the resource reservation hook and the IOAPIC identifier setup hook to their standard handlers.

The 32-bit graph caller preserves a small caller-saved set, derives the traced function address and a frame reference from the stack, adjusts for patched call size, delegates to prepare_ftrace_return, then restores registers and returns.

When an operations object already carries a trampoline that is not the graph special case FTRACE_GRAPH_ADDR, static resolution reports absence. Otherwise static resolution always yields an address derived from the register-aware or plain base.

Graph return handling is skipped when the current frame address indicates a non-virtual stack, when graph infrastructure reports itself dead, or when the current task has graph tracing paused. Otherwise tracing proceeds.

Early table allocation fails fast when the requested address lies outside the direct map or when the current page-table base is no longer the early top table. Exhaustion of the preallocated dynamic pool clears early tables and retries the walk from the top, and level folding applies when five-level paging is disabled.
Early large-page flags derive from __PAGE_KERNEL_LARGE without _PAGE_GLOBAL and without _PAGE_NX. Mode and shape state plus base addresses are fixed after initialization with four-level defaults.

Without physical address extension, each newly created second-level entry is mirrored into the kernel alias at the page-offset index, and ramdisk teardown clears both identity and alias entries across the recorded range. With the extension or without ramdisk support, teardown is a no-operation.

Early ramdisk state consists of a virtual start address plus a half-open range of second-level table slots covering the temporary mapping, populated during early table construction and consumed during teardown.

Legacy expectations default to keyboard controller present, real-time clock plus warm reset plus plug-and-play BIOS enabled, and BIOS region reservation disabled. Personal-computer hardware enables reservation, virtualized guests disable plug-and-play plus clock, and mobile-derived subarchitectures additionally mark the keyboard controller absent.

Early descriptor installation always covers the architectural exception range using early_idt_handler_array in vector order and loads idt_descr. Thirty-two-bit builds additionally cover remaining vectors with early_ignore_irq.
Idle trace targets and direct-trampoline defaults simply return to the caller, with call-depth accounting on 64-bit and weak linkage for the shared 32-bit stub to prevent assembler relaxation.

A trace operations object starts in static mode, may move to allocated mode with a stored trampoline base, and on release returns to a cleared base again resolving statically. Resolution checks allocation state on every query rather than caching.

The early top table early_top_pgt starts zeroed except for a reserved slot with a zero allocation cursor next_early_pgt and reloads the page-table base. Each missing intermediate level consumes one pooled page from early_dynamic_pgts and advances the cursor. Cursor reaching EARLY_DYNAMIC_PAGE_TABLES triggers a full reset and a fresh walk.

The 64-bit register caller inspects the saved original accumulator after the handler returns to select among normal restoration, updating the saved return address for direct-call requests, or reshaping the stack for tail-call requests with return-stack rebalancing.
Second-level table handling abstracts over paging mode by aliasing pl2_t plus pl2_base plus SET_PL2, selecting pmd_t with initial_pg_pmd in one build and pgd_t with initial_page_table in the other.

The 32-bit register entry builds a stack frame with reserved gaps plus saved segment selectors plus flags plus code segment plus captured address plus a zeroed original accumulator plus general registers, matching the layout expected for register-aware handlers.

The 64-bit trace entries share a compact saved-register area extended on demand with upper registers plus copied flags plus kernel data and code segments plus a reconstructed stack pointer, with frame-pointer encoding and a zeroed code-segment slot for operations lacking register support.

Runtime code modification for graph dispatch relies on a single-location text-poke primitive rather than an explicit lock visible in these fragments, implying external coordination for cross-CPU visibility.

Resuming from low-power sleep can reenter graph handling from early processor startup while still using a physical stack, so implementations must validate that the stack reference looks virtual before touching graph state to avoid faults.

A prefix of the 64-bit caller up to ftrace_caller_end is copied verbatim into generated trampolines, so changes to instruction choice or stack layout within that region alter every trampoline and require matching updates to offset calculations.

On-demand early mapping is only safe while still running on the early top table and for addresses inside the managed direct map; use after switching tables or for out-of-range addresses must take the fault path instead of installing entries.
The 32-bit entry must install the early exception table before any fault can occur, since later steps such as microcode loading and parameter sanitizing may themselves trigger exceptions.
ABI fact: patchable trace sites use the opcode constant JMP32_INSN_OPCODE together with the length constant MCOUNT_INSN_SIZE to define encoding and size.
ABI fact: early descriptor installation is bounded by the counts NUM_EXCEPTION_VECTORS for exceptions and NR_VECTORS for the full table on 32-bit.

ABI fact: early 32-bit construction uses PAGE_OFFSET and PGDIR_SHIFT for alias placement plus PTRS_PER_PTE for fanout plus PTE_PFN_MASK and PAGE_SIZE for address handling plus PDE_IDENT_ATTR and PTE_IDENT_ATTR for entry flags.

ABI fact: early 64-bit handling uses __PAGE_OFFSET and MAXMEM for range checks plus PTRS_PER_PGD and PTRS_PER_P4D and PTRS_PER_PUD and PTRS_PER_PMD for table sizes plus _KERNPG_TABLE for intermediate flags plus __START_KERNEL_map for address conversion plus X86_TRAP_PF and X86_TRAP_VC and X86_TRAP_VE for dispatch.
ABI fact: register-aware entries use __KERNEL_CS and __KERNEL_DS for segment state plus frame offsets RSP and RIP and EFLAGS and ORIG_RAX for field placement.
ABI fact: hardware subarchitecture selection uses X86_SUBARCH_PC and X86_SUBARCH_XEN and X86_SUBARCH_INTEL_MID and X86_SUBARCH_CE4100 to choose early setup and legacy expectations.

ABI fact: paging-mode defaults use USE_EARLY_PGTABLE_L5 as a build selector plus pgdir_shift and ptrs_per_p4d for shape plus page_offset_base and vmalloc_base and vmemmap_base for base addresses plus __pgtable_l5_enabled for mode state.
